public_rationale: The claim has three parts. The loss part holds: audited figures reported by the press put OpenAI's 2024 net loss attributable to the company at $5.09B, about $5B and at the top of his range (e1). The 'keeps losing money after converting' part also holds: after the restructuring, OpenAI reportedly posted a $9.3B operating loss in Q1 2026 (e4). The timing part fails. He said OpenAI would convert 'in the next six or so months', which means by roughly spring 2025. In May 2025 the conversion still had not happened and OpenAI revised the plan so the nonprofit kept control (e2). The restructuring into a for-profit PBC was completed on 2025-10-28, about 13 months after the post (e3). Some parts hold and one fails, so the outcome is mixed.
limitations: The 2024 loss figure comes from leaked audited statements reported by the press, not from a public OpenAI filing.
$5.09B is slightly above $5B. A stricter reading, or a loss measure taken before minority-interest allocation, would put the loss outside the range.
The post-conversion loss figures come from shareholder documents reported by The Information, and Reuters could not verify them.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI will lose $4–5 billion in 2024 and will keep losing money the same way after it converts to a for-profit.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI, a non-profit AI company that will lose anywhere from $4 billion to $5 billion this year, will at some point in the next six or so months convert into a for-profit AI company, at which point it will continue to lose money in exactly the same way.

from_speaker: "will lose anywhere from $4 billion to $5 billion this year" (2024)
"at some point in the next six or so months convert into a for-profit AI company"
"at which point it will continue to lose money in exactly the same way"
our_interpretation: The claim has three parts, and each is tested separately: (a) OpenAI's 2024 loss, (b) the conversion to a for-profit within about six months of 2024-10-02, (c) continued losses after conversion.

Part (a): the $4-5B range follows OpenAI's own projections as reported in the press. I read it as a ballpark. A reported 2024 net loss that rounds to about $5B meets it. A net loss far above $5B, or below $4B, does not.

Part (b): 'six or so months' read generously, through 2025-06-30. The forecast is met if the for-profit conversion was completed by then. A conversion completed much later does not meet the stated timetable.
Part (c): 'lose money in exactly the same way' read in the ordinary sense: the business kept running at an operating loss after conversion. It does not require identical figures.
The overall outcome is mixed if some parts hold and others fail.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI's reported 2024 net loss is about $4-5B, the for-profit conversion was completed by about mid-2025, and OpenAI kept losing money after it converted.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The reported 2024 loss is far outside $4-5B, or the conversion was not completed within about six months, or OpenAI turned profitable after converting.

evidence.explanation: Audited figures, verified by the FT, put OpenAI's 2024 net loss attributable to the company at $5.09B. That is about $5B, at the top of his $4-5B range.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI has decided that its nonprofit division will retain control over its for-profit organization, after the company initially announced that it planned to convert to a for-profit organization.
evidence.explanation: Seven months after the post, no conversion had happened and OpenAI had changed its plan. This fails the 'six or so months' timetable.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI has completed its recapitalization, simplifying its corporate structure. The nonprofit remains in control of the for-profit
evidence.explanation: The restructuring into a for-profit PBC was completed on 2025-10-28. That is about 13 months after the post, well past 'six or so months'.
In Q1 2026, after conversion, OpenAI reportedly posted a $9.3B operating loss. This supports the part saying it would keep losing money after converting.
